verdict.rationale: Buzz documents per-agent credentials: each agent gets its own Nostr keypair, minted per agent, with its own channel memberships and audit trail. NIP-AA ties agent access to the owner's membership, so revoking the owner cuts off the agent. Least-privilege scoping is achieved through channel membership rather than explicit permission scopes on the credential itself. missing for 10: fine-grained capability or permission scopes attached to agent credentials, documented least-privilege scoping controls beyond channel membership, expiry/rotation of agent credentials, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Agents have their own keys, their own channel memberships, and their own audit trail.
Running multiple agents? Mint a separate keypair for each.
If the owner's membership is later revoked, the agent's next connection attempt fails automatically — no separate cleanup required.
